description.narrative: The goal of the intervention is to improve quality of education in Albania by strengthening democratic citizenship education based on CoE standards and practices. Intermediate outcome is the following: The capacity of the Albanian education system to develop learners’ competences for a democratic culture, in line with national policy objectives and CoE instruments and approaches, is strengthened. Immediate outcomes are: 1. (Policy support) The policy and methodological framework on democratic citizenship education and the democratic governance of schools are aligned to key national education objectives and the Council of Europe standards and approaches. 2. (Democratic school governance) School children in selected schools are provided with the skills, knowledge and opportunities to participate in the decision-making processes in their schools and communities and engage in school and community-based projects jointly with civil society organisations. 3. (Teacher support) Teachers develop new professional competences, practices and attitudes that better contribute to the development of competences for democratic culture in learners and ensure an inclusive and enabling learning environment for all children.

Samarbetet med Council of Europe syftar till att stärka utbildningen i demokratiskt medborgarskap på grundval av Council of Europe normer och praxis. Målgrupperna är utbildningspolitiska beslutsfattare, lokalsamhällen, rektorer, lärare, elever och skolpersonal från utvalda grund- och gymnasieskolor i pilotsyfte. Delen av detta ingripande omfattar en omfattande granskning av utbildning i demokratiskt medborgarskap i Albanien för att identifiera möjligheter och utmaningar för att ytterligare anpassa den nationella läroplanen till Europarådets standarder och nationella politiska mål. Komponenten för demokratisk skolstyrning kommer att stödja 75 pilotskolor i att utveckla och genomföra politik och praxis för demokratisk styrning för att skapa en inkluderande och möjliggörande lärandemiljö för alla elever, med fokus på områden som digitalt medborgarskap, mediekompetens, säkerhet på nätet, bekämpning av mobbning, undervisning i kontroversiella frågor och klimatförändringar. Syftet med komponenten för lärarstöd är att förbättra lärarnas yrkesmässiga kompetenser, attityder och praxis genom e-lärande, regionalt kollegialt utbyte, utbildning och handledningsevenemang.

This cooperation with Council of Europe aims to strengthen democratic citizenship education based on Council of Europe standards and practices. The target groups are education policy makers, local communities, school principals, teachers, students and school staff from selected pilot primary and secondary schools. The Policy Support component of this intervention includes a comprehensive review of democratic citizenship education in Albania to identify the opportunities and challenges for further aligning the national curriculum to Council of Europe standards and national policy objectives. The Democratic School Governance component will support 75 pilot schools in developing and implementing democratic governance policies and practices to create an inclusive and enabling learning environment for all students, focusing on areas such as digital citizenship, media literacy, safety online, fighting bullying, teaching controversial issues, and climate change. The Teacher Support component aim at enhancing teachers’ professional competences, attitudes and practices through e-learning, regional peer exchange, training and coaching events.

title.narrative: Agreement Sida and Council of Europe

description.narrative:
- At the policy level, the project supported the implementation of Albanias National Education Strategy by strengthening safe, inclusive, and democratic school environments. A key achievement was technical support to the Ministry of Education in revising the citizenship curriculum for Grades 1, 6, and 10. The revised curriculum was officially approved and aligned with the Council of Europe's Reference Framework of Competences for Democratic Culture (RFCDC). It shifts learning from memorising civic knowledge to developing democratic values, attitudes, and critical thinking skills, supporting the strategy's competence-based education approach.
- The project aligned national priorities with the 2025 European Year of Digital Citizenship Education. An important institutional achievement was the official inclusion of 16 November as National Citizenship Education Day in the academic calendar. In higher education, a policy paper was drafted to integrate the Council of Europe's 10 Digital Citizenship Education domains into university governance and practice, promoting digital literacy and responsible online engagement.
- The project finalised the Guidelines for School Anti-Bullying Teams, supporting national efforts to prevent violence and create safer learning environments. It also provided technical assistance to the Ministry of Education on school financial autonomy, helping schools strengthen local decision-making and resource management.
- At school level, the Democratic School Governance network expanded to 80 pilot schools in 23 municipalities, exceeding the target of 75 schools. This expansion reflects strong demand for the Democratic School model. The procurement phase for 17 Democracy Labs was completed. Equipped with modular furniture and information technology, these spaces are expected to strengthen student participation, critical thinking, and community engagement.
- Awareness-raising initiatives contributed to positive changes in school culture. The Never Violence campaign, implemented with the Swedish Institute, reached approximately 4,000 visitors, while 2,955 students led activities addressing bullying in their schools. Following its official recognition, the first National Citizenship Education Day was marked by student-led activities promoting dialogue, tolerance, diversity, and inclusion.
- The Schools for Integrity initiative engaged more than 300 young people during Integrity Week 2025 through debates and public exhibitions focused on transparency and accountability. The Learning from the Past initiative, implemented with AIDSSH, involved 400 students in activities linking historical memory with civic responsibility.
- Student-led initiatives on integrity and transparency, anti-bullying, human rights, and digital citizenship continued to contribute to improvements in school culture. These activities promoted media literacy, democratic participation, academic integrity, and girls rights.
- Teacher capacity development remained a core element of the projects sustainability efforts. In 2025, 446 education professionals completed accredited training on anti-bullying, digital citizenship, participatory budgeting, and other priority themes.
